days.title: Choosing Models and Foundry Services: LLMs, Small Models, Reasoning, Multimodal Models and Foundry Tools

concepts.heading: Pick the Model Family by the Shape of the Task
concepts.body: Microsoft Foundry Models offers several families, and AI-103 asks you to choose by the job, not by brand. Reasoning models spend extra processing before they answer; Learn lists complex code generation, advanced problem solving and complex document comparison as their strengths, so they fit low-volume work where accuracy beats latency. General chat models answer quickly and handle drafting, summarizing and conversation. Small language models trade breadth for speed and cost on narrow tasks. Embedding models return vectors, not text, and power similarity search. Multimodal models accept more than one input type in one request. Before you deploy anything, open the model card in the Foundry model catalog and read its input and output types, its context window and the deployment types it supports in your region. A model that lists only text input can never look at the photo a user uploads, however large it is.

concepts.heading: Small Language Models and When to Scale Up
concepts.body: A small language model such as Phi-4-mini-instruct has far fewer parameters than a frontier model. It knows less about the world and is weaker at open-ended reasoning, but on a well-defined job, such as sorting a message into one of a few fixed labels or pulling one value out of short text, it can be accurate enough while answering faster and costing less per call. The signals that point to a small model are high volume, tight latency, short inputs and a closed set of outputs. Long documents, multi-step planning or broad world knowledge point to a larger model or a reasoning model. Do not switch production traffic on intuition: run an evaluation on a labeled sample of your own data against the current model, compare quality, latency and token use, then decide. The same rule applies when you consider fine-tuning, which shapes style and format but is not a reliable way to add facts.

concepts.heading: Multimodal, Vision and Audio Models
concepts.body: Learn shows Phi-4-multimodal-instruct with text, image and audio input and text output, while Phi-4 and Phi-4-mini-instruct take text only. Many Azure OpenAI chat models are vision-enabled, for example the GPT-4.1, GPT-4o and GPT-5 series and the o-series reasoning models, so a single request can carry a question and an image. For live spoken conversations, the Realtime API with gpt-realtime and the Voice Live API are generally available, while chat completions with gpt-audio still use a preview API version. Image generation has moved quickly: dall-e-3 retired on 2026-03-04, GPT-image-2 and the GPT-image-2.5 models are GA, and GPT-image-1, 1-mini and 1.5 are limited-access preview, so never pick a retired or preview model as the answer when a GA one fits. The first filter for any scenario with photos, scans or voice is always the input modality.

concepts.heading: Foundry Tools Versus Prompting a Model
concepts.body: Foundry Tools (formerly Azure AI services) are prebuilt APIs with a fixed output contract: Azure Speech for speech to text and text to speech, Azure Language for PII detection, language detection and named entity recognition, Azure Translator, Azure Content Understanding for turning documents, images, audio and video into a field schema with confidence and grounding, and Azure AI Content Safety. Use a tool when the result has a defined shape, such as a transcript, a list of PII entities with categories and offsets, or typed fields with a confidence score. Use a generative model when the output is new, open-ended language: drafting, explaining or combining sources. Status matters here too: Azure Language key phrase extraction, sentiment and opinion mining and summarization are now legacy features (retiring 2029-03-31), while PII, language detection and NER are core, so a new design should not rest on the legacy ones.

concepts.heading: Model Router: One Deployment, Many Models
concepts.body: Model router is a trained model that you deploy like any other Foundry model. For each request it looks at the prompt, its complexity and the kind of task, and sends it to a suitable underlying model: easy prompts go to smaller, cheaper models and hard ones to stronger or reasoning models. Your code calls one deployment name. Routing modes tune the trade-off: Balanced (the default) picks the most cost-effective model within a small quality range of the best, Cost accepts a wider quality band to save more, and Quality always picks the highest-rated model. You can also limit routing to a model subset, for example only the models your compliance team approved. Two side effects matter: the effective context window is that of the smallest model in the set, and sampling settings such as temperature are ignored when a reasoning model is picked. Model router is GA; its session affinity and routing metadata are preview.

examPoints: A question that describes volume, latency, input type and how open-ended the output is is testing model choice: small model for narrow high-volume work, reasoning model for accuracy-first analysis, multimodal model when images or audio arrive.

A question that contrasts a prebuilt Foundry Tool with prompting a chat model is testing the fixed-output-contract rule: transcripts, PII entities, translations and schema fields with confidence come from Foundry Tools, while drafting and synthesis come from models.
A question about mixed easy and hard prompts behind one endpoint is testing model router and its modes, model subset and smallest-model context limit, not custom routing code.

quiz.q: A support platform must detect the language of every incoming email and remove names, phone numbers and account numbers before the text is stored. The team already has a general chat model deployed. Which approach gives the most predictable result for this step?
choices: Prompt the chat model to detect the language and mask personal data, and ask it to return the masked text as a JSON object
Send each email to Azure Translator in Foundry Tools, because translating it to English first removes any personal data
Use Azure Language in Foundry Tools for language detection and PII detection, which returns redacted text and entities
Create a Content Understanding analyzer that generates a short summary of each email, so personal details never reach storage
quiz.explain: Language detection and PII detection are core Azure Language features with a fixed output contract, including entity categories and redacted text, which suits a compliance step. Choice A is tempting because the model is already deployed, but a prompt gives no guarantee of consistent categories or complete masking.

quiz.q: A company is planning two features: a nightly job that reads large multi-file bug reports and explains the most likely root cause, and an in-editor completion feature that must respond in a few hundred milliseconds. Which model pairing fits these requirements?
choices: A reasoning model for the nightly root-cause job, and a small fast model for the latency-sensitive completions
A small fast model for the nightly root-cause job, and a reasoning model with high effort for the completion feature
An embedding model for both features, because vector similarity finds both the root cause and the next line of code
One reasoning model at maximum effort for both features, because a single deployment is always cheaper to operate
quiz.explain: The nightly job is low volume and accuracy-first, which is the reasoning model case, while completion needs very low latency, which small models deliver. Choice D sounds simple, but reasoning effort adds latency and tokens to every completion request and breaks the response-time goal.

days.recap: Choose models by task shape and input modality, use Foundry Tools when the output has a fixed contract, check GA status before picking image or audio models, and use model router when one endpoint must serve both easy and hard prompts.

days.title: Retrieval, Indexing and Agent Knowledge: Search Modes, File Search, Foundry IQ, Memory and Tools

concepts.heading: Keyword, Vector and Hybrid Search
concepts.body: Azure AI Search offers three ways to match a query. Full-text (keyword) search ranks with BM25 and is best for exact tokens such as product codes, names, dates and error numbers. Vector search compares embeddings and finds conceptual matches even when no words are shared, the classic example being dog and canine. Hybrid search is a single request that carries both a search string and vectorQueries; the service runs both in parallel and merges them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) into one result list. On top of either, semantic ranker adds secondary (L2) ranking with language models adapted from Bing: it re-scores up to the top 50 results, returns @search.rerankerScore and can return captions and answers. Learn reports that hybrid retrieval with semantic ranking gives significant relevance gains in benchmarks, which is why it is the default recommendation for RAG. Scoring profiles and filters change ranking or scope; they do not add semantic understanding.

concepts.heading: Embeddings and Index Design
concepts.body: An embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small or text-embedding-3-large turns a chunk of text into a fixed-length vector. Two rules matter in every design. First, the index vectors and the query vector must come from the same embedding model; switching models means re-embedding the whole corpus. Second, with one multilingual embedding model a German question can find an English document, which language analyzers cannot do, because analyzers only improve keyword matching within one language. Large documents are split into chunks before embedding so that each vector represents a focused passage and only relevant chunks reach the prompt. Integrated vectorization lets an indexer chunk and embed content during indexing and vectorize query text at query time, so the application does not have to call the embedding model for every document. Keep a filterable field for anything you need to scope by, such as region, product line or the groups allowed to read the document.

concepts.heading: Choosing Knowledge for an Agent
concepts.body: Learn gives a rule of thumb for Foundry agents. The file search tool searches user-provided documents during an interaction: files go into a vector store that is chunked and embedded for you, and an agent and a conversation can each have at most one vector store attached. The Azure AI Search tool connects an agent to an existing, maintained index through a project connection; its query_type defaults to vector_semantic_hybrid and an OData filter applies to every query the agent sends. A Foundry IQ knowledge base grounds agents and apps on curated organizational content that several of them share. The web search tool uses Grounding with Bing Search for current public information with inline citations, but Learn notes the Microsoft Data Protection Addendum does not apply to data sent to it. Fine-tuning is not a way to add facts: it cannot cite sources and must be repeated whenever the content changes.

concepts.heading: Foundry IQ: What Is Generally Available
concepts.body: Foundry IQ is a managed knowledge layer built on Azure AI Search. You create a knowledge base that references one or more knowledge sources, and any app or agent calls its retrieve action. The GA surface is Search REST API 2026-04-01: knowledge bases with searchIndex, azureBlob, indexedOneLake and web knowledge sources, the intents input, and minimal, extractive retrieval that returns grounding content with references. Your own model then writes the answer. Still in preview: LLM query planning with non-minimal reasoning effort, answer synthesis inside the knowledge base, the multi-turn messages input, query-time ACL enforcement, SharePoint and other source types, and connecting a knowledge base to a Foundry agent through its MCP endpoint. The Foundry and Azure portals expose agentic retrieval through preview schemas. On the exam, a design that must use GA features only should call retrieve with intents and minimal effort and generate the answer itself.

concepts.heading: Memory and Tool Choices for Agents
concepts.body: Short-term memory is the current conversation: in Foundry Agent Service a conversation object stores the items of a chat and is passed on each response, and it lasts until you delete it. Long-term memory keeps distilled facts across sessions. Memory in Foundry Agent Service (user profile, chat summary and procedural memory) is in public preview, so a production design that must stay on GA features keeps cross-session preferences in its own store and supplies them to the agent, for example through a function tool. For actions, choose by where the code runs: the OpenAPI tool calls an API described by an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 spec from the service side, function calling lets your own application execute the call and return the output, the MCP tool reuses tools exposed by a remote MCP server, and code interpreter runs Python in a sandbox for calculations, data analysis and charts. Retrieval tools read content; they never change data.

examPoints: A question with exact codes plus natural-language questions, or with the best document stuck below the top three, is testing hybrid search with RRF and semantic ranker reranking.

A question about which knowledge option an agent should use is testing scope: file search for documents a user brings, the Azure AI Search tool for an existing index, Foundry IQ for shared curated content, web search for current public information.

A question that says GA features only is testing status: Foundry IQ retrieval on 2026-04-01 with intents and minimal extractive results is GA, while answer synthesis, query planning and Memory are preview.

quiz.q: A tutoring company wants its Foundry agent to remember each student's preferred explanation style across sessions over several months. Policy allows storing this preference, but production may use only generally available features. Which design fits?
choices: Enable Memory in Foundry Agent Service with user profile memory, so the agent extracts the preference automatically
Store each student's preference in the company's own database and supply it to the agent through a function tool
Keep every student's conversation open indefinitely, so the agent rereads all earlier sessions on each new question
Fine-tune a separate model for each student every month, so the preference becomes part of the model weights
quiz.explain: The app keeps the preference in its own store and hands it to the agent at run time, which works with GA features only. Choice A describes the feature built for this purpose, but Memory in Foundry Agent Service is still in public preview, so it does not meet the GA-only rule.

quiz.q: A hybrid query in Azure AI Search usually returns the most useful policy document somewhere in the top 40 results, but users only read the first three. The index and the embeddings are fine. Which change most directly improves the order of the top results?
choices: Raise the number of vector results returned by the query from 10 to 50, so more candidate chunks are included in the list
Add a scoring profile that boosts recently updated documents, so newer policy versions move to the top of the results
Switch the vector field to exhaustive KNN, so the nearest neighbors are calculated exactly instead of approximately
Enable semantic ranker on the query, which reranks the top results with language models and promotes the best matches
quiz.explain: Semantic ranker re-scores up to the top 50 results by meaning, which is exactly the problem of a good document ranked too low. Choice C is tempting because it sounds more precise, but exact nearest neighbors only change which vectors are found, not how well the merged list is ordered by relevance.

days.recap: Use hybrid search with semantic ranker for most RAG, embed content and queries with the same model, pick agent knowledge by scope, and keep Foundry IQ and memory designs on their GA surface.

days.title: Foundry Infrastructure: Resources, Projects, Networking, Deployment Types and CI/CD

concepts.heading: Foundry Resources, Projects and Topology
concepts.body: The Foundry resource (Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts, kind AIServices) is the top-level Azure resource: it holds networking, security settings and model deployments. A Foundry project (accounts/projects) is a development boundary inside it, where agents, files, evaluations and indexes live, while deployments and resource-level connections are shared with every project in that resource. New agent work starts on a Foundry project in the new portal; the current Agent Service is available only on Foundry projects, and hub-based projects remain the classic option for features such as prompt flow. Learn's rollout guidance describes two topologies. Co-located workloads share one resource with a project per use case, which suits experiments but shares quota, incidents and misconfiguration. Isolated workloads get one Foundry resource per production boundary, with independent access control, quota and cost. Some APIs, Translator for example, exist only at resource scope, so isolation for them requires separate resources.

concepts.heading: Network Isolation and Agent Setup
concepts.body: Learn splits Foundry network isolation into three directions. Inbound: set public network access to Disabled and add a private endpoint. Outbound to Azure services: use Private Link. Outbound from the agent runtime: virtual network injection into a subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments, /27 or larger, chosen when the Foundry resource is created; it cannot be added later or moved to another subnet without redeploying. Connected resources such as Storage, Azure AI Search and Cosmos DB keep their own governance, and Foundry does not create their private endpoints for you. Agent data has two setups. Basic setup stores conversations, files and vector stores in Microsoft-managed storage. Standard setup brings your own Azure Storage (files), Azure AI Search (vector stores) and Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL (conversations and agent definitions), declared through capability settings. Capability settings cannot be updated on an existing project, so decide before you create it. Multi-region availability means a Foundry resource per region with routing in the application; Foundry does not fail over on its own.

concepts.heading: Deployment Types and Options
concepts.body: Every Serverless API deployment has a deployment type that decides where inferencing runs and how you pay. Global types may process prompts in any Azure region; Data Zone types stay within the US, EU or APAC data zone; Standard and ProvisionedManaged stay in the resource's geography. Data at rest stays in the geography in every case. Standard types bill per token and suit bursty traffic; provisioned types reserve capacity in provisioned throughput units (PTUs) for steady, latency-sensitive volume; Batch types process large asynchronous files with a 24-hour target at a discount and use a separate enqueued quota, so they do not throttle live traffic. The Developer type is only for evaluating fine-tuned models. Serverless API is Learn's preferred option and supports data zone processing, customizable guardrails, keyless authentication and private networking with no hub. Managed compute is in preview, processes globally only and has no content filtering, so it is not the default answer.

concepts.heading: Configuring Model and Agent Deployments
concepts.body: Standard quota is granted per subscription, region, model and deployment type in tokens per minute; each deployment takes part of it through sku.capacity, measured in capacity units whose TPM value depends on the model. When the pool is used up, reduce another deployment of the same model or request more quota. The versionUpgradeOption controls model versions: OnceNewDefaultVersionAvailable follows each new default, OnceCurrentVersionExpired stays on your version until retirement and then moves to the default, and NoAutoUpgrade stops working at retirement. Provisioned deployments use in-place migration instead, which keeps the name and size while traffic moves. A deployment references its guardrail through raiPolicyName. Connections hold endpoints and authentication for other resources: create shared ones on the Foundry resource and team-only ones on the project. Prompt agents are versioned definitions (model, instructions, tools), and newly created agents get their own Entra agent identity, so role assignments on downstream resources must target that identity.

concepts.heading: Infrastructure as Code and CI/CD Pipelines
concepts.body: Learn's Bicep quickstart deploys accounts and accounts/projects, and the samples repository has templates for network isolation and standard agent setup. In Terraform, the AzureRM provider covers the resource, deployments, projects and connections, while the AzAPI provider reaches the full control plane, including capability hosts for bring-your-own resources; the two can sit side by side. Pipelines should sign in with Microsoft Entra ID: in GitHub Actions the Azure Login action with OpenID Connect uses a federated credential, so the repository stores no secret. When a template sets agent capability settings, the deploying identity also needs Storage Blob Data Contributor and Cosmos DB Operator on the referenced accounts; Azure AI Search needs no caller role. Keep prompt agent definitions in source control, create a new agent version on merge, and run an evaluation as a quality gate before production traffic moves.

examPoints: A question that weighs one shared resource against several is testing topology: projects in one resource share deployments, quota and blast radius, while a resource per production workload isolates access, quota and cost.

A question about residency, bursty versus steady traffic or overnight jobs is testing deployment types: Data Zone for zone residency, provisioned PTUs for steady latency-sensitive volume, Batch for delay-tolerant bulk work.

A question about a private agent network or a pipeline deployment is testing creation-time decisions: VNet injection and capability settings are fixed at creation, and pipelines use OIDC plus the extra provisioning roles.

quiz.q: A company created a Foundry resource last month without network settings. Security now requires the agent runtime to run inside the company's virtual network, using a subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments. What must the team do?
choices: Edit the existing Foundry resource and add the delegated subnet under its networking settings, then restart the agents
Create a private endpoint for the existing resource, because a private endpoint also moves the agent runtime into the VNet
Add a second project to the existing resource with the subnet selected, since injection is configured per Foundry project
Create a new Foundry resource with virtual network injection selected at creation, then recreate the projects and agents
quiz.explain: Learn states that virtual network injection is chosen when the Foundry resource is created and cannot be added to an existing resource. Choice B is tempting because private endpoints are part of the design, but they only control inbound access to the resource, not where the agent runtime makes its outbound calls.

quiz.q: A startup builds one agent application with dev, test and production environments. Production needs its own access control, quota and cost line, while dev and test can share model deployments to save effort. Which layout fits Learn's guidance?
choices: One Foundry resource with three projects, assigning the production team its roles on the production project only
A dedicated Foundry resource for production, and one shared Foundry resource with separate dev and test projects
Three hub-based projects on one hub, because each hub-based project receives its own model quota and budget
One Foundry resource for all three environments, with a separate Data Zone deployment for each of the environments
quiz.explain: Isolation by Foundry resource is the production default, and co-locating dev and test as projects in another resource keeps shared deployments where they help. Choice A is tempting because projects do separate agents and files, but projects share the resource's deployments and quota, so production would still share a blast radius with dev and test.

days.recap: Foundry projects live inside a Foundry resource, isolation for production comes from separate resources, network injection and agent capability settings are fixed at creation, deployment types set residency and billing, and pipelines deploy with Bicep or Terraform over OIDC.

days.title: Operating AI Workloads: Quotas, Rate Limits, Cost, Monitoring and Security

concepts.heading: Quotas and Rate Limits
concepts.body: A deployment's assigned TPM becomes its tokens-per-minute rate limit, and a requests-per-minute limit is derived from it. Unassigned quota helps nobody until you assign it, so a 429 that says the rate limit was exceeded while regional quota sits unused means the deployment itself is under-allocated. The limiter counts an estimate made when the request arrives: prompt tokens plus max_tokens (and best_of), not the tokens you are billed for. An oversized max_tokens therefore causes 429s even when usage metrics look low. RPM is enforced over short windows of about 1 or 10 seconds, so a burst at the start of each minute can be throttled although the minute's total is under the limit. Learn's client guidance: honor retry-after-ms when present, otherwise back off exponentially with jitter, cap retries, queue non-urgent work, and read x-ratelimit-remaining-requests and x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens to slow down before throttling starts. Failed requests still count against the limit.

concepts.heading: Scaling and Controlling Cost
concepts.body: For steady high volume, provisioned deployments reserve PTUs; when they are fully used they return 429, and spillover can send the overflow to a standard deployment of the same model and version in the same resource. Set spilloverDeploymentName on the provisioned deployment to cover every request, or send the x-ms-spillover-deployment header per request. Alert on Provisioned-managed Utilization V2, which throttles at 100 percent. To give each consumer its own limits on a shared model, put Azure API Management in front and use llm-token-limit with a counter key: tokens-per-minute returns 429 and token-quota over a period returns 403. Cost Management budgets only send alerts; they never block calls. Learn's cost traps: a deployed fine-tuned model is billed hourly for hosting even with no traffic, so delete idle ones; delay-tolerant bulk jobs belong on Batch; and smaller max_tokens and right-sized models cut both latency and spend. Group cost analysis by resource and meter to find the charge.

concepts.heading: Monitoring Models, Safety and Search Health
concepts.body: Azure Monitor collects Foundry platform metrics automatically. Useful ones include Azure OpenAI Requests split by StatusCode or IsSpillover, Time to Response for first-token latency, token metrics, and the Risks and Safety category: Blocked Volume counts calls the guardrail rejected, while Harmful Volume Detected also counts annotate-only detections. Agent telemetry, traces and evaluation results live in the Application Insights resource connected to the project; without that connection the portal views stay empty. Drift often comes from model version upgrades, so pin versions, test new ones in a side deployment and compare evaluation scores. For Azure AI Search, an indexer run marked Success can still have failed documents below Max failed items; read execution history or Get Indexer Status for per-document errors. HTTP 503 with a rising Throttled search queries percentage at query peaks calls for more replicas, while indexing pressure calls for partitions.

concepts.heading: Keyless Access and Secrets
concepts.body: API keys are static secrets with full access and no per-user identity. Microsoft recommends Microsoft Entra ID tokens for production workloads. Give the app a managed identity, use DefaultAzureCredential (your az login session locally, the managed identity in Azure) with the scope https://ai.azure.com/.default, and assign the Foundry User role on the project. Learn says not to use roles that start with Cognitive Services for Foundry work, apart from Cognitive Services Usages Reader for quota visibility. Keyless code alone leaves keys valid, so set disableLocalAuth to true or assign the built-in policy that requires key access to be disabled, then confirm an old key gets 401. For connections that still need secrets, Foundry stores them in a Microsoft-managed Key Vault by default; a bring-your-own Key Vault connection must be added before any other connection, one per resource, and deleting that vault breaks the resource.

concepts.heading: Private Networking and Role-Based Access
concepts.body: A private endpoint turns the public name into a CNAME to a privatelink subdomain and adds a private DNS zone linked to the VNet, so clients keep the same hostname. On-premises clients must forward the privatelink zone to a resolver that can read it, such as Azure DNS Private Resolver, or they get the public IP. Foundry roles: Foundry Agent Consumer only calls agent endpoints, Foundry User builds and tests in a project, Foundry Project Manager manages projects and publishes agents, Foundry Account Owner manages resources; Reader cannot call agents. The Azure portal assigns Foundry Agent Consumer only at account scope, so use the CLI for project or agent scope. Azure AI Search accepts only API keys by default: enable role-based access control, then grant Search Index Data Reader (query), Search Index Data Contributor (load) or Search Service Contributor (manage). An indexer reaching Blob Storage without secrets uses the search service's managed identity with Storage Blob Data Reader and a ResourceId connection string.

examPoints: A question with 429 errors is testing which limit is hit: the deployment's TPM or RPM allocation, max_tokens inflating the estimate, or short-window bursts, and the fix of backoff with retry-after-ms.
A question about overflow, per-team limits or unexpected cost is testing spillover, API Management llm-token-limit (429 versus 403) and hourly hosting of idle fine-tuned deployments.
A question about removing keys is testing managed identity with Foundry User, disabling local authentication, and turning on role-based access control with Search Index Data roles on Azure AI Search.

quiz.q: A batch client calls a standard deployment as fast as it can and starts receiving 429 responses after a few seconds of every minute. The team wants the client to slow down before it is throttled rather than after. What should the client read?
choices: The x-ratelimit-remaining-requests and x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens headers returned with every successful response
The Processed Inference Tokens metric in Azure Monitor, polled every few seconds from inside the batch client process
The usage object in each response body, comparing completion tokens with the quota shown on the Model quota page
The Activity Log of the Foundry resource, which records each throttled request together with the remaining capacity
quiz.explain: The remaining-requests and remaining-tokens headers report how much allowance is left on each response, so the client can pace itself before a 429. Choice C is tempting because it shows tokens, but the limiter counts prompt plus max_tokens at arrival, not billed completion tokens, so usage cannot predict throttling.

quiz.q: A web app calls a Foundry project with DefaultAzureCredential. It works on a developer laptop after az login, but in Azure App Service every call fails because no credential is available. Key authentication is disabled. What should the team do?
choices: Store a resource API key in an App Service app setting and pass it to the client whenever the token request fails
Assign the developer's user account the Foundry User role at the resource group scope that contains the web app
Enable a managed identity on the App Service and give that identity the Foundry User role on the project
Assign Cognitive Services Contributor to the App Service's outbound IP addresses on the Foundry resource itself
quiz.explain: In Azure, DefaultAzureCredential uses the app's managed identity, so the identity must exist and hold Foundry User on the project. Choice A is tempting as a quick fix, but key authentication is disabled, and Learn advises against Cognitive Services roles and stored keys for Foundry work.

days.recap: Rate limits come from the deployment's allocation and request estimates, cost and overflow are managed with Batch, spillover and API Management, monitoring runs on Azure Monitor and Application Insights, and security means managed identities, Foundry and Search roles, disabled keys and private endpoints with working DNS.

days.title: Responsible AI: Guardrails, Safety Evaluators, Red Teaming and Agent Governance

concepts.heading: Guardrails, Severity and Blocking Levels
concepts.body: Guardrails (previously content filters) use Azure AI Content Safety classifiers for four harm categories: hate and fairness, sexual, violence and self-harm. Each prompt and completion gets a severity of safe, low, medium or high. A control's blocking level says how much is blocked: Low blocks only high, Medium blocks medium and high, High blocks everything from low upward, and Off blocks nothing. Read it as how much is blocked, not as a minimum severity. Every model sold by Azure gets Microsoft.DefaultV2 by default: the four harms at Medium on prompts and completions, user prompt attack detection on prompts, and protected material for text and code on completions. Document attack detection is off by default. Any customer can turn a harm control off for input, but Off or annotate-only on output for the core harms requires approval for modified guardrails through a Limited Access review. Lower the blocking level to reduce false positives rather than turning controls off.

concepts.heading: Prompt Shields, Protected Material and Blocklists
concepts.body: Prompt Shields detects two attack types. User prompt attacks (formerly jailbreak) try to override system rules and are detected by default. Document attacks, or indirect prompt injection, hide instructions in third-party content such as emails, web pages or retrieved documents; you must add this control to a custom guardrail and, for model API calls, wrap untrusted documents in the documents delimiter inside the user message so the safety system can recognize them. Keep trusted instructions in the system message and never mix untrusted text into it. Spotlighting is a preview add-on, not a replacement. Protected material for text flags known prose such as lyrics and articles; protected material for code flags output matching public repository code and may be required for Customer Copyright Commitment coverage. Custom blocklists cover business terms no classifier knows, with exact or regex items on input, output or both; blocklist support is limited to Azure OpenAI models. A guardrail is an RAI policy resource assigned to deployments through raiPolicyName.

concepts.heading: Handling, Logging and Provenance
concepts.body: Applications must handle filtering explicitly. A blocked prompt fails with HTTP 400 and the error code content_filter, and the model never runs. In Chat Completions, a filtered completion returns HTTP 200 with finish_reason set to content_filter on the affected choice, and every response carries prompt_filter_results and content_filter_results with a severity and a filtered flag per category, even when nothing was blocked; the Responses API returns a top-level content_filters array instead. Logging these annotations with a request id gives an audit record of guardrail decisions. Treat such logs and traces as sensitive: redact personal data and never put secrets in prompts or span attributes. For agents, the trace of a run records each tool execution as an execute_tool span with its arguments and result, which is the evidence auditors ask for. For generated images, Azure OpenAI adds C2PA Content Credentials automatically: a signed manifest with fields such as AI Generated Image and the generating software, which tools such as the Content Credentials Verify page can read.

concepts.heading: Safety Evaluators and Red Teaming
concepts.body: Risk and safety evaluators score responses with Microsoft-hosted safety models, so no judge deployment is needed. The four content evaluators, builtin.violence, builtin.sexual, builtin.self_harm and builtin.hate_unfairness, use a 0-7 severity scale (very low 0-1, low 2-3, medium 4-5, high 6-7) and pass when the score is at or below the threshold, which defaults to 3. Each result includes a reason field that explains the score, which is the explanation tooling the study guide mentions. Other evaluators include builtin.protected_material, builtin.code_vulnerability for insecure code, builtin.indirect_attack for injected instructions, and builtin.ungrounded_attributes, which needs context. Prohibited actions and sensitive data leakage are preview evaluators for agent targets only. The AI Red Teaming Agent, built on PyRIT, generates adversarial prompts with attack strategies and reports attack success rate; it is preview, so use it to probe for weaknesses alongside the GA evaluators, not as the only release gate.

concepts.heading: Governing Agent Behavior and Approvals
concepts.body: Instructions are requests to the model, not controls. Enforce agent limits in configuration and code. On an MCP tool, allowed_tools restricts which server tools the agent may call, but an omitted or empty list allows every tool, so use a non-empty list. require_approval defaults to always and also accepts never, or per-tool lists such as never for read-only tools. When approval is needed, the response contains an mcp_approval_request item, and your app sends an mcp_approval_response with approve true or false and the matching approval_request_id in the same conversation. In Microsoft Agent Framework, mark risky function tools with approval_mode="always_require" in Python (ApprovalRequiredAIFunction in .NET) so the framework pauses until a person decides. Validate every model-generated function call, give each function the least privilege it needs, and log who approved what. Agent guardrails and the tool call and tool response intervention points are preview, so they add defense in depth rather than replace approvals.

examPoints: A question about legitimate content being blocked, or harmful content getting through, is testing blocking levels and the rule that Off or annotate-only on output for the core harms needs modified guardrail approval.
A question about hidden instructions in retrieved documents or emails is testing document attack detection, which is off by default and needs the documents delimiter around untrusted content.

A question about an agent that may change data is testing enforced controls: a non-empty allowed_tools list, require_approval with the approval request and response flow, and approval_mode in Agent Framework.

quiz.q: A team runs builtin.violence over a dataset with the default threshold. One response receives a score of 2. How does Foundry report this result?
choices: Fail, because any score above zero means the response contained some violent content that must be removed
Fail in the Medium band, because a score of 2 is closer to the threshold than to the safest possible score
Pass in the Low band, because the score is at or below the default threshold of 3 on the 0-7 scale
Pass with a quality rating of 2 out of 5, because violence uses the same scale as the coherence evaluator
quiz.explain: Content safety evaluators use a 0-7 scale where 2-3 is low, and a score at or below the default threshold of 3 passes. Choice D is tempting because 1-5 scales are common in Foundry, but those belong to AI-assisted quality evaluators, not to harm severity.

quiz.q: An agent uses an MCP server that exposes list_orders, get_order, cancel_order, refund_order and delete_customer. Reads must run unattended, cancellations and refunds need a person's approval, and delete_customer must never be callable. Which MCP tool configuration meets this?
choices: Leave allowed_tools empty and set require_approval to always, and tell the agent in its instructions never to call delete_customer
Set allowed_tools to the four order tools and set require_approval to never for list_orders and get_order only
Set allowed_tools to the four order tools and set require_approval to never, then log every tool call to Application Insights
Set allowed_tools to all five tools and set require_approval to always for delete_customer only, leaving the rest unattended
quiz.explain: A non-empty allowed_tools list hides delete_customer, and the per-tool never form lets reads run while every other allowed tool still waits for approval. Choice A is tempting because always sounds safest, but an empty list allows every tool, and an instruction does not enforce anything.

days.recap: Guardrails classify four harms by severity with blocking levels and DefaultV2 defaults, document attacks need explicit enabling, applications log annotations and handle content_filter results, safety evaluators score 0-7 against a threshold, and agents are governed with allowed tools and approvals, not instructions alone.

days.title: Consuming Models in Code: v1 API, Responses Versus Chat Completions, Keyless SDK and Multimodal Input

concepts.heading: Endpoints and SDKs
concepts.body: Two endpoints matter. The resource's v1 endpoint, https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/, is used with the standard OpenAI() client: pass it as base_url, and api_version is no longer required because v1 uses implicit versioning. It serves Azure OpenAI models and other models sold by Azure through Responses or Chat Completions, and it is the endpoint for embeddings. The project endpoint, https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>, is used by the Foundry SDK (azure-ai-projects): AIProjectClient handles project operations such as listing connections, and get_openai_client() returns an OpenAI-compatible client for responses, agents and evaluations. Learn notes the project endpoint does not currently route embedding requests. Anthropic Claude deployments use the Anthropic SDK and Messages API at https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic. In every case the model field carries your deployment name, not the catalog model name. A 404 from AIProjectClient usually means the URL is not in the project endpoint format.

concepts.heading: Keyless Authentication in the SDK
concepts.body: For Microsoft Entra ID authentication, Learn shows token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default") and then OpenAI(base_url=..., api_key=token_provider). The detail that catches people is that get_bearer_token_provider returns a function. Passing the function lets the client fetch and refresh tokens automatically; calling it once and passing the resulting string works until that token expires, after which every call fails with 401 until the process restarts. DefaultAzureCredential uses your az login session on a laptop and the managed identity in Azure, so the same code runs in both places. The identity needs a data-plane role: Foundry User on the project is the narrowest role for day-to-day development and for running evaluations, while Foundry Project Manager and Foundry Account Owner are for managing projects and resources. The AIProjectClient takes the same credential object directly.

concepts.heading: Responses and Chat Completions
concepts.body: The Responses API is the newer, stateful API with built-in tools; responses are stored by the service (by default for 30 days) so a later call can reference them. Carry context either with previous_response_id, sending only the new user input each turn, or by manual chaining, where the app appends response.output and the next message to its own input list and sends the whole list, which also works with store set to false. The Chat Completions API takes a message list and is supported by more models; if a deployment returns 400 Model not supported on Responses, call Chat Completions on the same v1 client. Structured outputs use text.format in Responses and response_format in Chat Completions; strict schemas need every property in required and additionalProperties false. With function calling, your app runs the function and returns a function_call_output with the matching call_id; strict functions need parallel_tool_calls false. tool_choice set to a named function forces that call, auto lets the model decide and none blocks calls.

concepts.heading: Multimodal Input
concepts.body: Vision-enabled chat models, including the GPT-4.1, GPT-4o and GPT-5 series and the o-series reasoning models, accept images in the same request as text. Instead of a plain string, the user message content becomes an array of parts: a text part with the question and an image_url part with the image. The URL must be reachable by the service; for a local or private file, Learn shows reading the bytes, base64-encoding them and passing a data URL of the form data:image/jpeg;base64,... in the image_url part. Sending the image directly is better than running OCR or captioning first, because OCR keeps only text and a caption loses the detail the question needs. Multiple images can go in one message for comparison. For live voice, use the GA Realtime API with gpt-realtime or Voice Live rather than a preview audio chat API version. Image input still passes through the deployment's guardrails, so harmful images can be blocked like harmful text.

concepts.heading: Reasoning Models and Background Mode
concepts.body: Reasoning models think before answering and do not accept every chat parameter: drop temperature, top_p and the penalty settings, use max_completion_tokens (Chat Completions) or max_output_tokens (Responses) instead of max_tokens, and tune reasoning_effort, low for fast simple calls and high for hard problems. The output budget includes hidden reasoning tokens, so size it generously and check for a status of incomplete; usage reports reasoning_tokens separately. Long reasoning tasks can run for minutes, which is fragile over a single HTTP call. Background mode solves this: send the Responses request with background=True, get a response id and a queued status at once, then poll responses.retrieve until the status is terminal, such as completed. Background mode requires store=True; stateless requests are not supported. To limit retained data, delete the stored response by id once your app has saved the result. Learn notes a known performance issue when combining background mode with streaming.

examPoints: A question with a 404, a 400 Model not supported or a failing embeddings call is testing which endpoint and API to use: v1 resource endpoint for OpenAI-style calls and embeddings, project endpoint for AIProjectClient, /anthropic for Claude.
A question where keyless calls work for a while and then fail with 401 is testing the token provider rule: pass the callable as api_key so tokens refresh.
A question about multi-turn state, privacy or minutes-long tasks is testing previous_response_id versus manual chaining and background mode, which requires store=True.

quiz.q: A financial app uses the Responses API for multi-turn chats. Policy says the service must not keep conversation data after each call, but the model must still see earlier turns. Which approach fits?
choices: Set store to true and pass previous_response_id on each turn, then rely on the default retention to remove the data later
Set store to false and manually chain turns by appending response.output and the next message to the app's input list
Set store to false and pass previous_response_id on each turn, so the service rebuilds the history from the earlier call
Create a new deployment for every chat session, so each model instance keeps the turns of one chat in its own memory
quiz.explain: Manual chaining keeps the history in the application and sends it each turn, so nothing has to stay stored by the service. Choice C is tempting because it looks shorter, but previous_response_id depends on a stored earlier response, which store set to false does not keep.

quiz.q: Inspection photos are stored in a private storage account that the model service cannot reach. A developer wants a vision-enabled deployment to answer questions about a specific photo. What should the request contain?
choices: A user message with a text part and an image_url part holding a base64 data URL built from the downloaded photo bytes
A user message with only a text part holding the private blob URL, so the model downloads the photo with its own access
A system message that includes the OCR text extracted from the photo, together with the question asked by the user
A function tool definition named get_photo, so the deployment can call the storage account on its own during inference
quiz.explain: Learn shows encoding a local image as a base64 data URL inside an image_url part, which needs no public URL. Choice C is tempting because it avoids the storage problem, but OCR keeps only text and discards the visual detail that an inspection question depends on.

days.recap: Call models through the v1 endpoint with OpenAI() or through the project endpoint with the Foundry SDK, pass a refreshing token provider for keyless auth, choose Responses or Chat Completions per model, send images as content parts, and use background mode with store=True for long reasoning tasks.

days.title: RAG in an Application: Classic RAG, Citations, On Your Data Retirement and Foundry IQ

concepts.heading: The Classic RAG Flow
concepts.body: Azure AI Search's RAG overview describes classic RAG: your application sends a query to Azure AI Search, takes the results and hands them to a model itself. A typical flow is: embed the user question with the same embedding model used for the index, run a hybrid query with semantic ranking, keep the top few chunks, and return only the fields you need with select. Then assemble the prompt: a system message that tells the model to answer only from the provided sources, to cite them and to say it does not know when they do not cover the question; the sources, each labeled with an id; and the user question. Classic RAG uses only GA features and gives you full control over retrieval, prompts and logging. Top-k and chunk size are the main levers for the token budget: too few chunks miss facts, too many waste tokens and dilute the answer. Dumping whole documents into the system message is never the answer.

concepts.heading: Citations and Fabrication Controls
concepts.body: In classic RAG the model can cite only what you show it, in the form you show it. Label each chunk with an identifier, for example [doc-17] Travel Policy v4: ..., and instruct the model to put the id after each claim. Models can still invent or mismatch ids, so the app keeps the list of ids it retrieved for the request and drops or flags any citation that is not in it before rendering links; Microsoft's migration checklist calls this validating citation ids. Inline citations next to each statement make unsupported claims easier to spot than a list of sources at the end, and an explicit not-found answer path removes the pressure to invent a rule. Lower temperature makes answers more consistent but does not ground them. Measure the result rather than trusting it: the Groundedness evaluator compares the answer with the retrieved context and penalizes content the context does not support, which is how you track fabrication over time.

concepts.heading: Scoping Retrieval and Security Trimming
concepts.body: Grounding must respect who may see what. Instructions such as only use documents for this user are not enforced; the model still sees whatever you retrieved. Enforce scope in the query. Add filterable fields to the index, for example region, product or a Collection(Edm.String) field of the group ids allowed to read each document (filterable, not retrievable), and build an OData filter from the signed-in user's groups on every query, such as group_ids/any(g:search.in(g, 'id1, id2')); Learn calls this the security filter pattern. Documents outside the filter never reach the prompt. Use keyless access from the backend: enable role-based access control on the search service and give the app's managed identity Search Index Data Reader, scoped to the index if possible. Built-in ACL and RBAC-scope enforcement in Azure AI Search, and query-time permissions in Foundry IQ, are still preview, so a GA design keeps trimming in its own filters. When migrating from an older managed grounding feature, remember that removing its configuration alone neither replaces retrieval nor preserves document-level authorization.

concepts.heading: On Your Data Has Retired
concepts.body: Azure OpenAI On Your Data let a chat completions request carry a data_sources block so the service queried a source such as Azure AI Search before answering. Learn now states that it retired on October 14, 2026 and is no longer supported; the article remains only for migration. Ordinary chat completions or Responses calls without that configuration are not affected, which is why plain chat keeps working. To find affected apps, search code, configuration and gateway logs for data_sources, the older dataSources, and the /extensions/chat/completions path. Removing the block alone is not a migration: nothing would retrieve documents, and the model would answer from training data. Supported replacements are classic RAG in your app, a Foundry IQ knowledge base called directly (Microsoft's migration sample reuses the existing index), or Foundry Agent Service with the Azure AI Search tool when tools and multi-turn agents are also needed. No api-version brings the retired feature back.

concepts.heading: Foundry IQ in an App: GA Scope
concepts.body: A Foundry IQ knowledge base wraps one or more knowledge sources, such as a search index, Blob Storage, OneLake or the web, and the app calls its retrieve action. In the GA REST API 2026-04-01, retrieve accepts the intents input and runs minimal, extractive retrieval: it returns merged grounding content with references, and your own deployed model writes the answer, citing those references. This suits several apps that need the same multi-source content defined once. LLM query planning with non-minimal reasoning effort, answer synthesis that returns a finished cited answer, and the multi-turn messages input are preview in 2026-08-01-preview, and the portals use preview schemas, so a compliance rule of GA only rules them out. For a Foundry agent that must ground on an index today with GA features, the Azure AI Search tool is the direct path, because connecting a knowledge base to an agent through its MCP endpoint is preview. Pick the surface first, then design the prompt and citations around it.

examPoints: A question about prompt assembly is testing classic RAG: hybrid plus semantic retrieval, top chunks with ids, an answer-only-from-sources instruction and a not-found path.

A question about data_sources, dataSources or /extensions/chat/completions is testing the On Your Data retirement on 2026-10-14 and its replacements: classic RAG, a Foundry IQ knowledge base or an agent with the Azure AI Search tool.

A question that requires GA only is testing Foundry IQ scope: retrieve with intents and minimal extractive results on 2026-04-01, while answer synthesis, query planning and messages input are preview.

quiz.q: A RAG app labels the five retrieved chunks doc-1 to doc-5 and asks the model to cite ids. An answer cites doc-9 for one of its claims. What should the application do before showing the answer?
choices: Show the answer unchanged, because the model may know doc-9 from its training data and the citation is probably correct
Send the same question again with a higher temperature, so the model is more likely to choose a different set of ids
Search the whole index for doc-9 and add it to the citations, because the model must have found a better document
Check cited ids against the five retrieved ids, and drop or flag the doc-9 citation and the claim that it supports
quiz.explain: The model only saw doc-1 to doc-5, so doc-9 is an invented citation, and validating ids against the retrieved set is the documented control. Choice C is tempting because it tries to rescue the citation, but the model never saw any doc-9, so the claim is not supported by what it read.

quiz.q: An internal assistant uses classic RAG over an Azure AI Search index of HR documents. Some documents are restricted to managers, and an employee received an answer quoting a manager-only policy. Each document has a filterable field listing the allowed group ids. What should the developer change?
choices: Add an instruction to the system message telling the model to ignore documents that the user is not allowed to read
Raise the semantic ranker threshold so manager-only documents rank lower for employees and drop out of the top results
Build an OData filter from the signed-in user's group ids and apply it to every search query before chunks reach the prompt
Move manager-only documents into a Foundry IQ knowledge base with answer synthesis, which hides restricted text automatically
quiz.explain: A security filter on the allowed groups field means restricted documents are never retrieved for that user, which is enforcement rather than a request. Choice A is tempting because it is quick, but the restricted text would still be in the prompt, and instructions do not reliably stop the model from using it.

days.recap: Classic RAG retrieves with hybrid and semantic search, labels chunks for citations the app validates, enforces access with query filters, replaces the retired On Your Data feature, and uses Foundry IQ only within its GA intents-and-extractive scope.

days.title: Evaluating Models and Apps: Quality, RAG and Textual Evaluators, Dataset Versus Model and Agent Targets

concepts.heading: How Evaluation Works in Foundry
concepts.body: An evaluation runs a set of evaluators over test data and reports scores, pass rates and per-row results. When you create one in the portal you first choose its target. A Model target runs a deployed model on your prompts and scores what it generates. An Agent target sends each test query to your agent and scores its responses, including tool calls. A Dataset target scores outputs you already have, so nothing is re-run: Learn describes it as evaluating preexisting outputs without re-running the model or agent. A Traces target scores agent interactions already captured in Application Insights. Data is a CSV or JSONL file, an existing dataset, or synthetic data generated by AI. Cloud evaluation from code uses the project endpoint: AIProjectClient, its OpenAI-compatible client, and criteria that name a builtin evaluator. Running evaluations needs at least the Foundry User role on the project.

concepts.heading: AI-Assisted Quality Evaluators
concepts.body: Coherence, Fluency, Relevance, Groundedness, Retrieval and Similarity are AI-assisted: a judge model reads the inputs and scores them from 1 to 5 with a default pass threshold of 3. Each needs a judge model deployment_name in its initialization parameters; without it the evaluator has nothing to call. Relevance checks whether the response addresses the query. Coherence judges logical flow and Fluency judges language quality, and Learn notes both are independent of factual correctness: a fluent, coherent answer can still be wrong. Groundedness compares the response with the grounding context and penalizes content the context does not support, which makes it the main fabrication detector for RAG. Response Completeness, the recall side that checks whether the answer misses facts in the ground truth, is preview. Pick the judge model deliberately; Learn's general-purpose guidance suggests a small current model such as gpt-5-mini as a balance of quality and cost.

concepts.heading: Evaluating the Retrieval Step
concepts.body: Learn splits RAG evaluation into system evaluation of the final answer (Groundedness, Relevance, Response Completeness) and process evaluation of retrieval. The Retrieval evaluator is AI-assisted and judges whether the retrieved context is relevant to the query; it needs query and context. Document Retrieval is for when retrieval quality is the bottleneck and you have human relevance labels. It compares retrieved_documents (ids with search scores) with retrieval_ground_truth (ids with query_relevance_label values) and returns standard search metrics: Fidelity, how many known good documents came back; NDCG and XDCG, ranking quality in the top results; Max relevance N; and Holes, retrieved documents with no label. It needs no judge model. Learn describes using it in a parameter sweep: generate results for different search algorithms, top_k values and chunk sizes and keep the settings with the best scores. Poor answers can come from poor retrieval or poor generation, and separate scores tell you which.

concepts.heading: Textual Similarity Metrics
concepts.body: When you have expected answers, two families compare the response with ground truth. Similarity (builtin.similarity) is an LLM judge that focuses on meaning rather than overlap and considers the query, so a correct paraphrase scores well; it needs query, response and ground_truth plus a judge deployment, scores 1-5 and defaults to a threshold of 3. F1, BLEU, GLEU, ROUGE and METEOR are algorithmic: they compute token or n-gram overlap, need no judge model, return a value from 0 to 1 and default to a threshold of 0.5. METEOR adds some synonym and stemming handling, and ROUGE needs a rouge_type. Learn's advice: use Similarity when paraphrases or synonyms should count as equivalent, and use the algorithmic metrics when exact token overlap is the criterion, such as machine translation quality, fixed-answer retrieval or NLP benchmarking. All six are GA. Overlap metrics punish reordered or reworded correct answers, which is a common exam distractor.

concepts.heading: Mapping Data and Planning Test Sets
concepts.body: Every evaluator reads named fields through a data mapping such as {{item.query}}, and a missing field means that evaluator cannot score the row. Required inputs: Relevance needs query and response; Coherence needs query and response or messages; Fluency needs only the response; Groundedness needs the response and the context, with the query optional; Retrieval needs query and context; Similarity needs query, response and ground_truth; the overlap metrics need ground_truth and response. Decide which metrics matter before collecting data: log the retrieved context with each answer if groundedness matters, and write expected answers if you want Similarity or F1. To compare a new model version with the current one, run a Model target evaluation against each deployment on the same prompts and compare scores, then switch production. Add safety evaluators to the same run so the release review sees quality and risk together, and keep the dataset in source control so later runs are comparable.

examPoints: A question about scoring last month's logged answers, versus testing a new model or agent, is testing evaluation targets: Dataset scores existing outputs, while Model and Agent targets generate new ones first.
A question about fabricated details in RAG answers is testing Groundedness, which needs the response and the retrieved context, not Coherence or Fluency, which ignore factual correctness.
A question about which evaluator can run on a given file, or why one failed to start, is testing required fields and the judge deployment_name for AI-assisted evaluators.

quiz.q: A team has a JSONL file in which each line holds a query, the app's response and the retrieved context, but no expected answers. Which evaluator cannot score these rows?
choices: Similarity, because it compares each response with a ground truth answer that the file does not contain
Groundedness, because it needs the query, the response and the retrieved context for every single line
Retrieval, because it scores how relevant the retrieved context is to the query that was asked by the user
Relevance, because it judges whether each response addresses its query, using only those two fields
quiz.explain: Similarity requires ground_truth, which the file lacks, while the other three need only fields that are present. Choice B is tempting because Groundedness sounds demanding, but it needs only the response and the context, with the query optional, and both are in the file.

quiz.q: Before upgrading production, a team wants to compare a new model version with the current one on the same 300 prompts, scoring freshly generated answers for relevance and groundedness. Which evaluation setup fits?
choices: A Dataset target over last month's logged answers, because it scores outputs without running any model again
A Traces target over the production Application Insights data, because it already holds the current model's answers
An Agent target with synthetic data, because generated questions give a broader view than the team's own prompts
A Model target run against each of the two deployments with the same 300 prompts, then a comparison of the scores
quiz.explain: A Model target generates new answers from each deployment on identical prompts, so the scores compare the two versions directly. Choice A is tempting because it avoids inference, but logged answers all came from the current model, so they say nothing about the new version.

days.recap: Choose the evaluation target first, score answers with AI-assisted evaluators that need a judge deployment, separate retrieval quality from answer quality, use Similarity for paraphrases and overlap metrics for exact wording, and plan test data around each evaluator's required fields.

days.title: Agents I: Foundry Agent Service, Instructions, Tools and Conversations

concepts.heading: Agents, Versions, Conversations and Responses
concepts.body: In Foundry Agent Service a prompt agent is defined entirely by configuration: a model deployment, instructions and tools. You author it in the portal or with the SDK or REST API, which lets you keep it in source control; each change creates an immutable agent version. Hosted agents are for your own code and framework, such as Agent Framework or LangGraph, shipped as a container image that Foundry runs with a managed endpoint and its own Entra identity; choose them only for custom orchestration or protocols. Runtime state uses three objects: the agent, a conversation that stores the items of a multi-turn exchange (messages, tool calls, outputs), and a response, one invocation created with responses.create and the conversation id. A response without a conversation is a single independent turn. The classic assistants, threads, messages and runs model is deprecated and retires on 2027-03-31; when migrating, threads become conversations and runs become responses.

concepts.heading: Instructions, Tool Policy and Availability
concepts.body: Instructions define the agent's role, goals, boundaries and output format, and they are where you say which tool to use when. When tools overlap, for example file search and web search both answering a policy question, add a decision rule such as use File Search for company policy and Web Search only for public information, and say what to do when a tool returns nothing. If grounded answers come back without citations, the first fix Learn lists is an instruction that explicitly requires citations; when streaming, also read the url_citation annotations. If the model does not call a tool you need, set tool_choice to required for deterministic behavior and review the traces. Tool availability has two conditions: the model and the region must both support the tool, so a tool not supported error despite a supported model usually means the region lacks it. Clear tool and parameter descriptions are the fix when a tool is called with wrong arguments.

concepts.heading: Knowledge Tools: File Search and Azure AI Search
concepts.body: File search reads from vector stores. An agent-level vector store holds content every conversation should see, such as a handbook, and a conversation-level vector store holds files a user brings to one chat; each can have at most one attached. Vector stores created through conversation helpers expire seven days after they were last active, and requests on that conversation then fail until you recreate and reattach the store. Limits include 512 MB per file and 10,000 files per vector store; poll new agent-level files until processing completes. The Azure AI Search tool connects to an existing index through project_connection_id and index_name, with optional top_k (default 5), query_type (default vector_semantic_hybrid) and an OData filter applied to every query. For keyless access, use a project connection with authType AAD and grant the Foundry managed identity Search Index Data Contributor and Search Service Contributor; with private networking, key-based connections are not supported.

concepts.heading: Action Tools: Function Calling, OpenAPI and MCP
concepts.body: Function calling: the model returns a function_call item, your application runs the code and submits a function_call_output. Runs expire 10 minutes after creation, so slow work should return a job id at once and be checked by a second function. The portal can run agents with function tools but cannot add or edit function definitions or execute them, so configure and test functions from code. The OpenAPI tool calls an API described by an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 spec from the service side; every operation needs an operationId made of letters, hyphens and underscores only, and authentication is anonymous, API key, or project managed identity with the audience that the target API expects. The MCP tool calls a remote MCP server endpoint; the runtime cannot reach a local server, so host it on Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions. Store MCP credentials in a project connection referenced by project_connection_id, never in code or the server URL.

concepts.heading: Code Interpreter and Content Understanding
concepts.body: Code interpreter runs Python in a sandboxed session for calculations, data analysis and charts. Each conversation that uses it gets its own session, which is active for one hour by default with a 30-minute idle timeout, so download generated files promptly and keep them in your own storage. Generated files come back as container_file_citation annotations on the output message, carrying a container_id and a file_id; the app downloads them with the containers files API rather than parsing the reply text. Code interpreter has charges beyond model tokens. When an agent needs exact, typed fields from documents, such as a policy number and an amount from a scanned claim form, retrieval tools are the wrong fit because they return chunks the model must interpret. Call an Azure Content Understanding analyzer with a field schema, typically through a custom function tool, and return its JSON fields with confidence as the function output, so the agent can pass reliable values to the next API.

examPoints: A question about keeping multi-turn context or migrating classic agents is testing conversations and responses: create a conversation, pass its id on every responses.create call, and map threads to conversations and runs to responses.

A question about which tool lets an agent act is testing where the code runs: function calling in your app with a 10-minute run limit, OpenAPI from the service with a valid spec, MCP over a remote endpoint with a project connection.
A question about missing citations, wrong tool choice or a tool not supported error is testing instructions with decision rules and the model-and-region availability rule.

quiz.q: An agent must look up loyalty points through an internal library that only the company's own web application can load. The library has no REST API or OpenAPI specification. How should the developer expose this lookup to the agent?
choices: Add the OpenAPI tool with a handwritten specification, so the service can call the internal library on its own
Add the code interpreter tool and upload the library, so the sandbox can import it and run the lookup itself
Define a function tool; the app runs the library call itself and returns a function_call_output
Add the Azure AI Search tool over an index of loyalty balances, which the agent queries before each answer
quiz.explain: Function calling lets the model request the lookup while the application, which can load the library, runs it and returns the output. Choice A is tempting because the OpenAPI tool avoids client code, but the service calls a reachable HTTP API, and this library is not exposed as one.

quiz.q: A user asks a code interpreter agent for a chart, leaves, and comes back two hours later to download it, but the file can no longer be retrieved. What explains this, and what should the app do?
choices: The vector store attached to the conversation expired, so the app should recreate it with the same files and reattach it
The code interpreter session has ended, so the app should download generated files promptly and store them itself
The agent version changed during the break, so the app should pin the agent version that was used when the chart was made
The chart was only described in the reply text, so the app should ask the model to encode the image as base64 text next time
quiz.explain: Code interpreter sessions are active for one hour by default with a 30-minute idle timeout, so files must be downloaded through the container files API while the session lives. Choice A is tempting because expiry fixes exist for vector stores, but those hold searchable files, not the outputs that code interpreter generates.

days.recap: Prompt agents are versioned configurations that run through conversations and responses, instructions decide tool use, file search and the Azure AI Search tool ground answers, function calling, OpenAPI and MCP perform actions, and code interpreter and Content Understanding handle computation and structured extraction.

days.title: Agents II: Multi-Agent Orchestration, Approvals, Tracing and Agent Evaluation

concepts.heading: Multi-Agent Options in Foundry Agent Service
concepts.body: The Connected Agents tool from the classic Agents API is not available in the new Foundry Agent Service. Learn names two replacements: the A2A tool and workflows. The a2a tool type uses the Agent2Agent protocol v1.0 and is generally available; the older a2a_preview type for v0.3 stays in preview. The calling agent sends a request to a remote A2A endpoint, the remote agent processes it and returns a response, and the calling agent uses it while it keeps managing the conversation. A Foundry agent becomes a callable A2A endpoint only when you enable incoming A2A: an agent card describing its capabilities plus the A2A protocol enabled on the agent endpoint, set together in one PATCH call. All A2A URLs require Microsoft Entra ID, and the caller needs Foundry Agent Consumer or another role with endpoint access on the target project or agent. Requests that do not name a version get v0.3, which is preview, so select v1.0 for production.

concepts.heading: Orchestration Patterns in Microsoft Agent Framework
concepts.body: Microsoft Agent Framework is the direct successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen, built by the same teams, with migration guides from both; Python and .NET are the main languages. Its workflows connect agents and functions through explicit execution paths, with state for long-running and human-in-the-loop scenarios. Patterns: sequential for fixed stages that each need the previous output; concurrent for independent analyses of the same input that run in parallel and are aggregated; handoff, where control passes directly between agents and the receiver takes full ownership and context; group chat, where a central orchestrator picks the next speaker; and Magentic, where a planning manager coordinates agents on open-ended tasks (its .NET types are still marked experimental; Learn suggests group chat when no complex planning is needed). The simpler agent-as-tool approach keeps a primary agent in charge: it delegates a subtask, gets the answer back and remains responsible. Learn's design advice is to use the simplest option that works: a single model call for a single-step task, one agent with tools next, and multi-agent orchestration only when the problem needs it.

concepts.heading: Portal Workflows Are Retiring
concepts.body: Workflows in the Foundry portal are a visual, declarative builder that orchestrates agents with templates for human in the loop, sequential and group chat patterns, logic nodes, Power Fx expressions, a YAML view and versioning. They are preview, and Learn states that Microsoft Foundry is retiring workflows on December 1, 2026, telling new builds to use Microsoft Agent Framework; a migration guide exists for existing workflows. Hosted agents are not supported in the workflow designer. For an exam scenario that starts new orchestration work, the retirement alone rules the designer out, whatever its features. Agent Framework workflows run in your own application or inside a Foundry hosted agent and can use Foundry models and tools. Long-running workflows run in supersteps and save checkpoints at the end of each one, including pending approval requests; InMemoryCheckpointStorage is for tests, FileCheckpointStorage for one machine, and CosmosCheckpointStorage for production, distributed runs that must survive restarts and redeploys.

concepts.heading: Approvals and Safeguards in Autonomous Flows
concepts.body: Semiautonomous agents need enforced checkpoints for consequential actions. For MCP tools in Foundry Agent Service, require_approval returns an mcp_approval_request item that your app shows to a person and answers with an mcp_approval_response, approve true or false, using the request's id in the same conversation. In Agent Framework, mark a function with approval_mode="always_require" in Python or wrap it in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction in .NET; the run stops with a request for user input that contains the function name and arguments, and the decision is passed back in a new run. Handoff workflows support approval-required tools, and checkpoints keep a pending approval alive across restarts, which matters when a manager approves two days later. Reflection or maker-checker loops, where one agent drafts and another checks against explicit criteria, need a maximum number of iterations so they cannot bounce forever. Record every approval with the person, tool, arguments and decision next to the trace.

concepts.heading: Tracing, Monitoring and Agent Evaluation
concepts.body: Foundry tracing uses OpenTelemetry and stores traces in the Application Insights resource connected to the project. Server-side tracing turns on automatically once Application Insights is connected and covers what runs in Foundry; tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents.
