A question that compares Content Understanding with Document Intelligence is testing the decision guide: variable documents and inferred fields favor Content Understanding, while fixed templates and air-gapped containers favor Document Intelligence.

quiz.q: An insurer wants a Document Intelligence custom extraction model for claim forms from 30 hospitals. Each hospital uses its own layout, and fields move around between form versions. Which model type should the team train first?
choices: A custom template model, because it relies on one consistent visual template shared by every hospital's form
The prebuilt receipt model, because its merchant and total fields map directly to hospitals and claim totals
A custom neural model, because it handles structured, semi-structured and unstructured documents and layouts
The read model alone, because it returns every word on each page and so removes the need for custom training
quiz.explain: Custom neural models handle varied layouts, and Learn recommends starting with them. Choice A is tempting because both custom types use the same labelling process, but template models depend on a consistent visual layout, which these forms don't have.

quiz.q: A digitization team needs only the plain text of scanned letters, without tables, figures, summaries or fields, at the lowest cost. No chat or embedding model is deployed in the Foundry resource. Which Content Understanding analyzer fits?
choices: prebuilt-documentSearch, because its Markdown summary of each letter gives the cleanest possible plain text
prebuilt-read, because it returns OCR text such as words and paragraphs and needs no language model at all
prebuilt-digitalParse, because it reads the internal text layer of each scanned page faster than OCR does
A custom analyzer based on prebuilt-image, because image analyzers are optimized for text-heavy scanned pages
quiz.explain: prebuilt-read gives OCR text without layout analysis or generative steps, so it needs no model deployment. Choice C is tempting because it avoids OCR, but scanned letters have no machine-readable text layer, and Learn points scans to read or layout instead.

days.recap: Use Content Understanding analyzers to turn files into clean Markdown and typed fields (documentSearch for RAG, read and layout for extraction only, custom analyzers with classify, generate and extract plus confidence), run them asynchronously on mapped deployments under inherited guardrails, and choose Document Intelligence for fixed templates and air-gapped containers.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: AI-103 gives you 120 minutes, and you pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Microsoft doesn't publish the number of questions, so pace yourself by time and check at the halfway mark that you are about halfway through. The domains are plan and manage an Azure AI solution 25 to 30 percent, implement generative AI and agentic solutions 30 to 35 percent, and computer vision, text analysis and information extraction 10 to 15 percent each, so more than half the exam is planning, generative AI and agents. Microsoft says you may have interactive components to complete; try the exam sandbox to see the item types. The audience is developers with Python experience, so expect short code, SDK calls and request settings. Most questions cover GA features, and commonly used preview features may appear, but a key answer for a production need shouldn't rest on preview features such as Sora 2, agent Memory, model router routing metadata or knowledge base answer synthesis. Use current names: Microsoft Foundry, Foundry Tools, guardrails (previously content filters) and the Foundry User role.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Planning, Generative AI, and Agents
concepts.body: Guardrails enforce safety on inputs and outputs; a system message only steers. Prompt Shields detect attacks, harm controls classify hate, sexual, violence and self-harm, and blocklists match terms in text. File search grounds on documents a user brings to one conversation, the Azure AI Search tool uses an existing index, and a Foundry IQ knowledge base serves curated knowledge to many agents. Structured outputs go in response_format for Chat Completions and in text.format for the Responses API. temperature steers non-reasoning models; reasoning_effort and the output token budget steer reasoning models. Prompt caching reuses input prefixes and never caches answers, and model router picks a model per prompt, unlike a load balancer. Sequential orchestration chains dependent steps, concurrent runs independent views in parallel, and handoff passes control at run time. Status traps: Azure OpenAI On Your Data retired on 14 October 2026; classic threads, messages and runs retire on 31 March 2027 in favor of conversations and responses; Foundry portal workflows retire on 1 December 2026, with Microsoft Agent Framework as the code path; the A2A tool is GA.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Vision, Language, Speech, Search, and Extraction
concepts.body: In an image edits mask, transparent pixels change and opaque pixels stay; generations creates new images and edits changes existing ones. gpt-image-2 is GA, the gpt-image-1 family is limited access preview, dall-e-3 is retired and Sora 2 is preview. Image detail low reads one 512x512 version, and high adds tiles for small text. Content Credentials are signed metadata, not a visible mark. Azure Language core features (PII, language detection, NER, health) differ from legacy ones (sentiment, key phrases, summarization, CLU). Translate changes the language, Transliterate changes the script; NMT suits volume, LLM translation suits tone. Phrase lists and custom speech fix recognition, lexicons fix pronunciation. Fast transcription is synchronous for files, batch is asynchronous for volume, and real-time streams. Embedding skills work at indexing time, vectorizers at query time. Hybrid scores are RRF ranks, while semantic reranker scores run from 0 to 4. Content Understanding infers fields from variable documents; Document Intelligence suits fixed templates and air-gapped containers.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: In the last days, understanding the questions you missed helps more than answering new ones. Keep an error log with three columns: the topic, the rule you didn't know, and the clue in the stem you should have noticed. For example: topic structured outputs, rule an optional field is required plus null, clue "phone is optional"; or topic hybrid search, rule RRF scores are tiny, clue "cutoff tuned for cosine". After each practice set, add rows, reread the whole log, and redo missed questions a day later without looking at the answer. Add a fourth column for status when you picked a preview or retired feature by mistake, because Foundry changes fast and many traps rest on GA status. Group entries by domain to see which day of this plan to revisit; generative AI and agents carry the largest weight, so give that domain extra time if the log is spread evenly. Use the question bank's domain filter and the mock exam's one section option to drill a weak domain, and stop adding new material the evening before the exam.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan
concepts.body: The day before, run a short timed mock, reread your error log and sleep. On the day, check your ID and testing setup early; for an online proctored exam, clear the desk and run the system test ahead of time. If the exam isn't available in your preferred language, Microsoft lets you request an additional 30 minutes. During the exam, read the last sentence of each scenario first, then look for the deciding clue: GA only, production, least engineering effort, lowest latency, no labelled data, private network or keep the layout. Eliminate answers built on retired items such as dall-e-3 or On Your Data, on retiring services such as Image Analysis 4.0 or Custom Vision for new designs, and on preview features when the stem demands GA. For code and request snippets, check where each setting lives before judging the logic. If a question takes too long, choose your best answer, mark it for review and move on, and answer every item. If you don't pass, review the score report by domain; after a first failure Microsoft requires a 24-hour wait before a retake, then 14 days between later attempts, up to five attempts in 12 months.

examPoints: A question that offers both a GA option and a preview or retired one for a production need is testing status knowledge: gpt-image-2 over gpt-image-1 or dall-e-3, extractive knowledge base retrieval over answer synthesis, and transcribe-then-reason over preview audio chat.
A question with one deciding clue, such as no labelled data, keep the layout, browser client or private network, is testing whether you read for that clue before choosing among look-alike services.

quiz.q: A company's design review allows only GA features in production. It needs product banners from text, RAG retrieval through an Azure AI Search knowledge base, and analysis of recorded support calls. Which set of choices meets the rule?
choices: gpt-image-1 for banners, knowledge base retrieval with answer synthesis, and gpt-audio chat completions on calls
gpt-image-2 for banners, extractive retrieval on REST 2026-04-01, and fast transcription then a chat model
dall-e-3 for banners, the messages input for knowledge base retrieval, and batch transcription then a chat model
Sora 2 still frames for banners, LLM query planning on the knowledge base, and Voice Live on recorded call files
quiz.explain: gpt-image-2, extractive knowledge base retrieval on 2026-04-01 and a transcribe-then-reason pipeline are all GA. Choice A is tempting because each item works technically, but gpt-image-1 is a limited access preview, answer synthesis is preview, and gpt-audio chat completions use a preview API version.

quiz.q: A browser-based voice assistant built on a gpt-realtime deployment feels laggy, and it starts answering whenever users pause briefly in the middle of a sentence. Which pair of changes addresses both problems?
choices: Connect over SIP from the browser, and add the users' filler words to a phrase list so pauses are ignored
Connect over WebSocket from each browser, and raise max_output_tokens so replies wait for the whole turn
Connect through batch transcription callbacks, and set turn_detection to none so the server can't interrupt
Connect over WebRTC from the browser client, and set turn_detection to semantic_vad in session.update
quiz.explain: WebRTC is Learn's recommended low-latency method for browser clients, and semantic_vad ends a turn based on meaning rather than silence. Choice B is tempting because WebSocket is a supported method, but Learn positions it for server-to-server use with higher latency, and output tokens have nothing to do with turn detection.

days.recap: AI-103 is 120 minutes with a scaled pass mark of 700 and an unpublished question count; weight your review toward planning, generative AI and agents, drill the confused pairs and GA versus preview status, read each scenario for its deciding clue, and answer every item before submitting.
